tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

66	/-- Adding an active authority derived from `src`, within its footprint and held by a live holder,
67	preserves `WF3` (§49), including §49.4 (the new footprint consists of leaves of the source) and
68	§49.7 (root authorities are unchanged). -/
69	private theorem addAuth_wf3 {s : S3} (hwf : WF3 s) {src : Nat} {x : Authority} {m : Mode}
70	    {fp : List Nat} {hd : Holder} (hx : s.A[src]? = some x) (hfp : ∀ p ∈ fp, p ∈ x.footprint)
71	    (hl : HolderLive s hd) : WF3 (s.addAuth ⟨m, some src, fp, hd, true⟩) := by
72	  have hs := lt_of_getElem? hx
73	  have live := HolderLive.congr (addAuth_P s ⟨m, some src, fp, hd, true⟩) rfl rfl
74	  have usable := fun q =>
75	    S3.Usable.congr (q := q) (addAuth_P s ⟨m, some src, fp, hd, true⟩) rfl rfl
76	  refine ⟨hwf.frames, hwf.places, ⟨hwf.owners.1, hwf.owners.2.1, fun q hq => ?_⟩, ?_, ?_,
77	    rootChain_addAuth hwf.rootChain hx rfl hfp,
78	    hwf.rootHeld.transport rfl (fun r => (usable r).1)
79	      (fun i z hz _ _ => by rw [addAuth_lt (lt_of_getElem? hz)]; exact hz), ?_⟩
80	  · obtain ⟨f, hf, hfF⟩ := hwf.owners.2.2 q ((usable q).1 hq)
81	    exact ⟨f, (FrameOf.congr (addAuth_P s _)).2 hf, hfF⟩
82	  · intro a y hy l hl'
83	    rcases addAuth_get hy with ⟨-, hy'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
84	    · exact hwf.footprints a y hy' l hl'
85	    · exact hwf.footprints src x hx l (hfp l hl')
86	  · intro b y a hb ho
87	    rcases addAuth_get hb with ⟨-, hb''⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
88	    · exact hwf.origins b y a hb'' ho
89	    · cases ho; exact hs
90	  · intro a y hy ya
91	    rcases addAuth_get hy with ⟨-, hy'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
92	    · exact (live _).2 (hwf.holders a y hy' ya)
93	    · exact (live _).2 hl

221	whole `split` (§61 effect: one authority per region, added in order). -/
222	private theorem split_induct {src : Nat} {x : Authority} (Q : S3 → Prop)
223	    (step : ∀ (s : S3) (r : List Nat), Q s → s.A[src]? = some x → (∀ p ∈ r, p ∈ x.footprint) →
224	      Q (s.addAuth ⟨.modify, some src, r, .frame s.top, true⟩)) :
225	    ∀ (rs : List (List Nat)) (s : S3), Q s → s.A[src]? = some x →
226	      (∀ r ∈ rs, ∀ p ∈ r, p ∈ x.footprint) → Q (splitEff s src rs)
227	  | [], s, hq, _, _ => by simpa [splitEff] using hq
228	  | r :: rs, s, hq, hx, hr => by
229	    rw [splitEff_cons]
230	    exact split_induct Q step rs _ (step s r hq hx (hr r (List.mem_cons_self ..)))

232	      fun r' hr' => hr r' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hr')

239	      rs.Pairwise (fun r r' => ∀ l ∈ r, l ∉ r') → I1 (splitEff s src rs)

241	  | r :: rs, s, h1, hx, hr, hpw => by
242	    rw [splitEff_cons]
243	    have hs := lt_of_getElem? hx
244	    have h1' := addAuth_I1 (hd := .frame s.top) h1 hx fun p hp => by
245	      rw [hr r (List.mem_cons_self ..) p hp]; exact Mode.le_refl _
246	    obtain ⟨hpr, hpw⟩ := List.pairwise_cons.1 hpw
247	    refine split_i1_aux rs _ h1' (by rw [addAuth_lt hs]; exact hx) (fun r' hr' p hp => ?_) hpw

342	/-- Adding an authority not covering `p` keeps the effective mode of `src` on `p`, through the
343	whole `split` (§43, §61 effect). -/

345	    ∀ (rs : List (List Nat)) (s : S3), s.A[src]? = some x → (∀ r ∈ rs, p ∉ r) →
346	      effective (splitEff s src rs) src p = effective s src p
347	  | [], s, _, _ => by simp [splitEff]
348	  | r :: rs, s, hx, hp => by
349	    have hs := lt_of_getElem? hx
350	    rw [splitEff_cons, split_effective_notin rs _ (by rw [addAuth_lt hs]; exact hx)
351	      (fun r' hr' => hp r' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hr')),
352	      effective_addAuth_notin hs (hp r (List.mem_cons_self ..))]

354	/-- An absent effective mode stays absent when an authority is added (§43, case 1 or 3). -/
355	private theorem effective_addAuth_none {s : S3} {y₀ : Authority} {a p : Nat} (ha : a < s.A.length)
356	    (h : effective s a p = none) : effective (s.addAuth y₀) a p = none := by
357	  unfold effective at h ⊢
358	  rw [addAuth_lt ha]
359	  cases hx : s.A[a]? with
360	  | none => rfl
361	  | some x =>
362	    rw [hx] at h; simp only at h ⊢
363	    split
364	    · rename_i hc
365	      rw [ite_eq_left hc] at h
366	      rw [descModes_addAuth]
367	      unfold effOf at h ⊢
368	      by_cases h0 : descModes s a p = []
369	      · rw [ite_eq_left h0] at h; cases h
370	      · rw [ite_eq_right h0] at h
371	        by_cases hm : Mode.modify ∈ descModes s a p
372	        · rw [ite_eq_right (fun e => h0 (List.append_eq_nil_iff.1 e).1),
373	            ite_eq_left (List.mem_append_left _ hm)]

377	/-- Adding a `Modify` authority derived from `src` and covering `p` removes the effective mode of
378	`src` on `p` (§43, case 3). -/
379	private theorem effective_addAuth_desc {s : S3} {src p : Nat} {r : List Nat} {hd : Holder}
380	    (hs : src < s.A.length) (hp : p ∈ r) :
381	    effective (s.addAuth ⟨.modify, some src, r, hd, true⟩) src p = none := by
382	  unfold effective
383	  rw [addAuth_lt hs]
384	  cases hx : s.A[src]? with
385	  | none => rfl
386	  | some x =>
387	    simp only
388	    split
389	    · rw [descModes_addAuth, ite_eq_left ⟨rfl, hp, by rw [ancs_addAuth_self rfl hs]; exact
390	        List.mem_cons_self⟩]
391	      unfold effOf
392	      rw [ite_eq_right (fun e => List.cons_ne_nil _ _ (List.append_eq_nil_iff.1 e).2),
393	        ite_eq_left (List.mem_append_right _ (List.mem_singleton_self _))]

396	/-- After a `split`, `src` has no effective mode on a leaf of a region (§43, case 3, §61 effect). -/
397	private theorem split_effective_in {src p : Nat} :
398	    ∀ (rs : List (List Nat)) (s : S3), src < s.A.length →
399	      (effective s src p = none ∨ ∃ r ∈ rs, p ∈ r) → effective (splitEff s src rs) src p = none
400	  | [], s, _, h => by
401	    rcases h with h | ⟨r, hr, -⟩
402	    · simpa [splitEff] using h
403	    · cases hr
404	  | r :: rs, s, hs, h => by
405	    rw [splitEff_cons]
406	    refine split_effective_in rs _ (by simp only [S3.addAuth, List.length_append]; omega) ?_
407	    rcases h with h | ⟨r', hr', hp⟩
408	    · exact .inl (effective_addAuth_none hs h)
409	    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 hr' with rfl | hr'
410	      · exact .inl (effective_addAuth_desc hs hp)
411	      · exact .inr ⟨r', hr', hp⟩

414	effective mode of `src` is unchanged; on a leaf of a region (distributed), it becomes absent, so in
415	particular `src` loses effective `Modify` there. -/

418	    ((∀ r ∈ rs, p ∉ r) → effective s' src p = effective s src p) ∧

421	  obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := hp.active
422	  exact ⟨split_effective_notin rs s hx, fun hin =>
423	    split_effective_in rs s (lt_of_getElem? hx) (.inr hin)⟩

448	/-- An authority after a release is an authority before, with the same fields, active only if it
449	was active and is not the released one (§62 effect). -/
450	private theorem release_back {s : S3} {a : Nat} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x) {j : Nat}
451	    {z : Authority} (hz : (releaseEff s a).A[j]? = some z) :
452	    ∃ z₀, s.A[j]? = some z₀ ∧ z.mode = z₀.mode ∧ z.origin = z₀.origin ∧
453	      z.footprint = z₀.footprint ∧ z.holder = z₀.holder ∧
454	      (z.active = true → z₀.active = true ∧ j ≠ a) := by
455	  rw [release_get hx] at hz; split at hz
456	  · subst_vars; cases hz; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, by simp⟩
457	  · exact ⟨z, hz, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun hz' => ⟨hz', Ne.symm ‹_›⟩⟩

460	(§62 effect). -/
461	private theorem release_fwd {s : S3} {a : Nat} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x) {j : Nat}
462	    {z : Authority} (hz : s.A[j]? = some z) :
463	    ∃ z', (releaseEff s a).A[j]? = some z' ∧ z'.mode = z.mode ∧ z'.origin = z.origin ∧
464	      z'.footprint = z.footprint ∧ z'.holder = z.holder := by
465	  rw [release_get hx]; split
466	  · subst_vars; rw [hx] at hz; cases hz; exact ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
467	  · exact ⟨z, hz, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩

470	private theorem effAnchorOK_release {s : S3} {a : Nat} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
471	    (e : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : EffAnchorOK (releaseEff s a) e fd ↔ EffAnchorOK s e fd := by
472	  have he : (releaseEff s a).effAnchor e = s.effAnchor e := by
473	    simp only [S3.effAnchor, release_ancs hx]
474	  have hH : (releaseEff s a).hframe = s.hframe := funext (S3.hframe_congr (release_P s a))
475	  unfold EffAnchorOK
476	  rw [he, hH, release_F, release_get hx]
477	  split
478	  · rename_i h; rw [← h, hx]; exact Iff.rfl
479	  · exact Iff.rfl

485	/-- `release` preserves `WF3` (§49, §62): it changes only the activity of a derived authority, so
486	footprints (§49.4) and active root authorities (§49.7) are unchanged. -/
487	theorem release_preserves_wf3 {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} (hw : WF3 s)
488	    (h : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s')) : WF3 s' := by
489	  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
490	  obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := hp.active
491	  have hder : x.origin ≠ none := by have := hp.derived; rw [hx] at this; exact this
492	  have hP := release_P s a
493	  refine ⟨by rw [release_F, release_nF]; exact hw.frames,
494	    by rw [hP, release_dead]; exact hw.places,
495	    ⟨by rw [hP, release_nF]; exact hw.owners.1, by rw [hP]; exact hw.owners.2.1, fun q hq => ?_⟩,
496	    fun b y hb l hl => ?_, fun b y o hb ho => ?_,
497	    hw.rootChain.transport (by rw [hP]) (by rw [hP]) (fun _ => by rw [release_ancs hx])
498	      (fun b y' hb => by obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, -, -, e', -⟩ := release_back hx hb; exact ⟨y₀, hy₀, e'⟩)
499	      (fun i z hz hzo => by
500	        obtain ⟨z', hz', -, e1, e2, -⟩ := release_fwd hx hz; exact ⟨z', hz', e1.trans hzo, e2⟩),
501	    hw.rootHeld.transport hP (fun _ hu => release_usable.1 hu) (fun i z hz _ hzo => ?_),
502	    fun b y hb ya => ?_⟩
503	  · obtain ⟨f, hf, hfF⟩ := hw.owners.2.2 q (release_usable.1 hq)
504	    exact ⟨f, (FrameOf.congr hP).2 hf, by rw [release_F]; exact hfF⟩
505	  · obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, -, -, e', -⟩ := release_back hx hb
506	    rw [hP]; exact hw.footprints b y₀ hy₀ l (e' ▸ hl)
507	  · obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, -, e', -⟩ := release_back hx hb
508	    exact hw.origins b y₀ o hy₀ (e' ▸ ho)
509	  · rw [release_get hx]; split
510	    · rename_i e; subst e; rw [hx] at hz; cases hz; exact absurd hzo hder
511	    · exact hz
512	  · obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, -, -, -, eh, ea⟩ := release_back hx hb
513	    rw [eh, HolderLive.congr hP (release_F s a) (release_dead s a)]
514	    exact hw.holders b y₀ hy₀ (ea ya).1

522	  obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀, m₁, -, f₁, -, ac₁⟩ := release_back hx ha'

532	  intro b y o hb ho
533	  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, m₀, e', f₀, -⟩ := release_back hx hb
534	  obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hm, hh⟩ := h2 b y₀ o hy₀ (e' ▸ ho)

538	/-- `release` preserves I3 (§52, §62.3, §62.4): no usable place but the holding place keeps the
539	released authority as anchor, and the effect removes it from the holding place. -/
540	theorem release_preserves_i3 {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} (h3 : I3 s)
541	    (h : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s')) : I3 s' := by

551	    have := hp.anchors q (List.mem_range.2 hq'.lt) hq' hy'

605	/-- Restoration of rights by `release` (§62 effect, §26, §32): if `b`, derived from `a`, is the
606	only active descendant of `a` covering `p`, then before the release `a` has no effective mode on `p`
607	when `b` is a `Modify` authority covering `p`, and after it the effective mode of `a` on `p` is its
608	own mode. -/
609	theorem release_restores_authority {s s' : S3} {b a p : Nat} {y x : Authority} (hw : WF3 s)
610	    (h : ReleaseStep b s (.ok s')) (hy : s.A[b]? = some y) (ho : y.origin = some a)
611	    (hx : s.A[a]? = some x) (xa : x.active = true) (xp : p ∈ x.footprint)
612	    (honly : ∀ j z, s.A[j]? = some z → z.active = true → p ∈ z.footprint → a ∈ s.ancs j →
613	      j = b) :
614	    (y.mode = .modify → p ∈ y.footprint → effective s a p = none) ∧
615	      effective s' a p = some x.mode := by
616	  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
617	  obtain ⟨y', hy', ya⟩ := hp.active
618	  rw [hy] at hy'; cases hy'
619	  have hab : a < b := hw.origins b y a hy ho
620	  have hanc : a ∈ s.ancs b := by
621	    unfold S3.ancs; rw [chain_cons (by simp [S3.org, hy, ho]) hab]; exact List.mem_cons_self ..
622	  refine ⟨fun hm hpy => ?_, ?_⟩
623	  · rw [effective_eq hx xa xp]
624	    have hmem : Mode.modify ∈ descModes s a p := mem_descModes.2 ⟨b, y, hy, ya, hpy, hanc, hm⟩
625	    unfold effOf
626	    rw [ite_eq_right (List.ne_nil_of_mem hmem), ite_eq_left hmem]
627	  · have hx' : (releaseEff s b).A[a]? = some x := by
628	      rw [release_get hy, ite_eq_right (Nat.ne_of_lt hab).symm]; exact hx
629	    rw [effective_eq hx' xa xp]
630	    have hnil : descModes (releaseEff s b) a p = [] := by
631	      apply nil_of_forall_not_mem; intro e he
632	      obtain ⟨j, z, hz, za, zp, hj, -⟩ := mem_descModes.1 he
633	      rw [release_ancs hy] at hj
634	      obtain ⟨z₀, hz₀, -, -, ef, -, ea⟩ := release_back hy hz
635	      exact (ea za).2 (honly j z₀ hz₀ (ea za).1 (ef ▸ zp) hj)
636	    rw [hnil]; rfl

672	
673	namespace SplitWithoutDD
674	
675	/-- A contract declaring every pair of regions disjoint (§61.3), which violates `DDSound` (§80);
676	its other components are irrelevant to `split`. -/
677	def KDD : K := ⟨fun _ _ => True, fun _ => False, fun _ => False, fun _ => False, fun _ => False,
678	  fun _ _ => False, fun _ _ _ => False⟩
679	
680	/-- Decidability of `KDD.DeclaredDisjoint` (§61.3). -/
681	instance : ∀ r r', Decidable (KDD.DeclaredDisjoint r r') := fun _ _ => instDecidableTrue
682	
683	/-- One static root leaf, `Init`, owned by the base frame (§47). -/
684	def cst : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true)]
685	
686	/-- The initial state of `cst` (§47). -/
687	def cs0 : S3 := S3.init cst
688	
689	/-- The places of `cs0` (§47). -/
690	theorem cs0_P : cs0.P = [⟨none, .frame 0, 0⟩] := by decide
691	
692	/-- The authorities of `cs0`: the root authority of place 0 (§47). -/
693	theorem cs0_A : cs0.A = [⟨.modify, none, [0], .frame 0, true⟩] := by decide
694	
695	/-- The only element of a singleton list (§38: identities are list indices). -/
696	private theorem get_one {α : Type} {a v : α} : ∀ {q : Nat}, [a][q]? = some v → q = 0 ∧ v = a
697	  | 0, h => by simp at h; exact ⟨rfl, h.symm⟩
698	  | _ + 1, h => by simp at h
699	
700	/-- `cs0` satisfies the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57). -/
701	theorem cs0_kInv : KInv cs0 := by
702	  have hP := cs0_P
703	  have hA := cs0_A

/-!
# Access kernel: the preserved invariant

The conjunction that every kernel step must preserve (§57 of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`) and the auxiliary invariant carried with it. The per-operation preservation modules state their results with these two predicates.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The kernel invariant of §57: `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`. -/
def KInv (s : S3) : Prop := WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s

/-- Auxiliary invariant carried with `KInv`, not a clause of §57 (§40, §49.7): the converse
root-holder property `RootHeldConv`, which is not a clause of `WF3`. -/
def KAux (s : S3) : Prop := RootHeldConv s

/-- `NoOrphan` follows from `WF3` (§54, §49.7), so `KInv` reduces to its first three
conjuncts. -/
theorem kInv_of {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hi : Inv3 s) (ha : AnchorOrderHeld s) : KInv s :=
  ⟨hw, hi, ha, noOrphan_of_wf3 hw⟩

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

# I. Safe-Behavior Contract

The following contract applies to all safe code and all properly encapsulated abstractions, regardless of their concrete memory representation.

## 1. Definitions of Safe Behavior

**Safe operation:** An operation that imposes no unchecked safety obligation on its user whose violation could compromise the language's guarantees.

**Safe code:** Code that executes only safe operations and does not directly assume obligations specific to unsafe operations.

**Safe interface:** An interface whose every permitted use preserves the language's guarantees when its implementation is correct.

**Safe abstraction:** An abstraction exposing a safe interface; its implementation may use unsafe operations provided it fulfills all their obligations.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.
## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations (O9–O11) do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid: every authority of its origin chain, its effective anchor included, is active.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights

These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.

/-- `derive` preserves I2 (§51, §60.1, §60.2): the derived mode does not exceed the own mode of the
source, whatever the region, and the region is within the footprint of the source. -/
theorem derive_preserves_i2 {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {region : List Nat} {m : Mode} (h2 : I2 s)
    (h : DeriveStep src region m s (.ok s')) : I2 s' := by
  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨x, hx, -, hm⟩ := exercisableAt_mode hp.exercisable
  exact addAuth_i2 h2 hx hm fun p hp' => afp_eq hx ▸ hp.within p hp'

/-- `release` preserves I2 (§51, §62.3, §62 effect): origins, modes and footprints are unchanged,
and the released authority is the origin of no active authority, since it has no active
descendant (§62.3) and, under `WF3` (§49.5), an origin is an ancestor. Without `WF3`, an origin
chain that does not decrease hides the active child from §62.3 (report of the v0.1 kernel
reconstruction). -/

    (h : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s')) : I2 s' := by
  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  obtain ⟨x, hx, -⟩ := hp.active
  intro b y o hb ho
  obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, m₀, e', f₀, -, ea⟩ := release_back hx hb
  have ho₀ : y₀.origin = some o := e' ▸ ho
  obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hm, hh, hact⟩ := h2 b y₀ o hy₀ ho₀
  obtain ⟨x₁', hx₁', em, -, ef, -⟩ := release_fwd hx hx₁
  refine ⟨x₁', hx₁', by rw [m₀, em]; exact hm, fun p hp' => by rw [ef]; exact hh p (f₀ ▸ hp'),
    fun ya => ?_⟩
  have y₀a := (ea ya).1
  rw [release_get hx] at hx₁'
  split at hx₁'
  · rename_i e; subst e
    have hanc : a ∈ s.ancs b := by
      unfold S3.ancs
      rw [chain_cons (by simp [S3.org, hy₀, ho₀]) (hw.origins b y₀ a hy₀ ho₀)]
      exact List.mem_cons_self ..
    exact absurd ⟨y₀, hy₀, y₀a⟩
      (hp.noActiveDesc b (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy₀)) hanc)
  · rw [hx₁] at hx₁'; cases hx₁'; exact hact y₀a
